quotes.text: we constructed a dataset containing nine core tables based on MIMIC-IV v3.1
we linked scenario tasks from Stage II with clinically similar existing patients

rationale: The paper names MIMIC-IV v3.1, describes an EHR-style database platform/schema, and reports linking scenario tasks to patient records. This provides a route from task to source record through patient/task linkage.

quotes.text: Patient data were derived from MIMIC-IV, a publicly available, de-identified dataset compliant with HIPAA regulations

rationale: The benchmark states data origin and IRB/HIPAA/de-identification status. It does not document data licence or terms separately enough for full credit.

quotes.text: selected patients with complete records across all tables, yielding a cohort of 49,419 patients

rationale: The paper reports a sampling/filtering design and cohort size. It does not compare patient features against a named target population.

searched: S1 paper/appendix, S2 README/docs, S3 release notes, S4 code, S5 agent-visible prompts/tool descriptions. The packet reports risks and limitations but no dedicated unsafe-output test or bias test.

searched: S1 paper/appendix, S2 README/docs, S3 release notes, S4 code, S5 agent-visible prompts/tool descriptions. No developer-side contamination controls such as gated access, canaries, encryption, held-out sets, or overlap checks are reported.

searched: S1 paper/appendix, S2 README/docs, S3 release notes, S4 code, S5 agent-visible prompts/tool descriptions. The packet does not state that agents are isolated from ground-truth results at run time or name an isolation mechanism.

quotes.text: a Google Search server with search and fetch tools for retrieving up-to-date medical references

rationale: Some data are versioned or specified, but evaluation depends on live external Google Search and API model services. Therefore the environment is not fully frozen.

quotes.text: referenced all elements against patient information through item-by-item review and correction

rationale: The paper reports manual verification and correction of task answers, calculator names, outputs, and inputs. It does not report a scripted reference solution run through the grader.

searched: S1 paper/appendix, S2 README/docs, S3 release notes, S4 code, S5 agent-visible prompts/tool descriptions. The described tools support database reads, search/fetch, and Python computation; no task changes environment state.

quotes.text: Tasks encompass multiple procedural steps and branching decisions

rationale: The benchmark gives a design argument that tasks require multi-step and branching work, making trivial success unlikely. No empirical random/trivial-agent or chance rate is reported.
searched: S1 paper/appendix, S2 README/docs, S3 release notes, S4 code, S5 agent-visible prompts/tool descriptions. No do-nothing or random-agent result is reported.

quotes.text: Table 9 reports per-dimension agreement rates,, and Cohen’s Kappa

rationale: The benchmark validates its automatic extraction/evaluation step on its own outputs and reports agreement, kappa, and correlation figures. This satisfies the full validation anchor.

searched: S1 paper/appendix, S2 README/docs, S3 release notes, S4 code, S5 agent-visible prompts/tool descriptions. The paper mentions default hyperparameters but does not report seeds, temperature 0, or a repeated-run policy.

quotes.text: scenario planning combined with tool-augmented training significantly improves performance

rationale: The paper makes a significance-style comparison claim without reporting a statistical test or confidence interval for the headline model comparison. Under the anchor, unsupported 'significant' language receives at most partial credit.

quotes.text: We used the default hyperparameters unless otherwise specified.

rationale: The paper reports a sampling/decoding policy only as default hyperparameters. It does not state the number of runs per task or independence of runs.

rationale: The benchmark reports a JSON action schema and documents read-only behavior for the SQL tool, with side-effect information reaching an agent-visible tool description. Complete documented return semantics including failures for every tool are not fully reported.

rationale: The README provides a tool-server verification command and expected successful execution. It does not disclose simulated/stub/no-op behavior or show such a disclosure reaching the agent-visible surface.

support using DeepSeek-V3.1 as a cost-effective and reproducible extractor

rationale: The grader input is the trajectory-derived final calculators, numerical results, and SQL fields, and the paper gives a rationale for using the extractor. It does not validate on injected correct/incorrect state changes with per-class error rates.

searched: S1 paper/appendix, S2 README/docs, S3 release notes, S4 code, S5 agent-visible prompts/tool descriptions. No controls on answer leakage through tools, retrieval, web access, held-out labels, canaries, or provenance markers are reported.

quotes.text: The evaluation encompassed model performance across four clinical domains

rationale: The paper reports results by clinical domain, a named benchmark axis. It does not report results by patient demographic subgroup or slice sizes with the slice results.

a publicly available, de-identified dataset compliant with HIPAA regulations and approved by an institutional review board

rationale: The environment state is reported as mixed real de-identified MIMIC-IV data and synthesized records, with HIPAA/de-identification and IRB status. Separate redistribution terms for environment data are not stated.
